Specifically, we truncate the questions in a survey dataset and feed them as input to LLMs for completion. Additionally, we use the base version of LLMs instead of the instruction fine-tuned version to have a more accurate representation of the data contamination problems in the pre-training data of these models. Finally, we compute the length of the longest common sequence (LCS) between the prediction of LLMs and the ground truth completion. The sequence here is defined as a sequence of words. The data contamination rate of one test sample (the survey question) is then calculated as the ratio of the length of LCS and the length of the ground truth prediction.
